# GitTurtle patch to gpui-pre-macros 0.3.4

This directory contains the exact crates.io `gpui-pre-macros` 0.3.4 source under Apache-2.0, the version the matching GPUI Kit 0.6.0 stack locks. `LICENSE-APACHE` is byte-for-byte preserved. The registry archive checksum is `e29384b3145f0143a17187b35339779398fe4c1d4534320d6a05594248a49965`; the package metadata names Zed's `crates/gpui_macros` at `69164008341295ad481bb11c0334a712ca8c23e3` (`https://github.com/zed-industries/zed`). `Cargo.toml` is the published normalized manifest and dependency requirements are unchanged; the workspace lockfile pins their versions. The registry-only `.cargo-ok` and the package lockfile are omitted. Apart from this note, `src/test.rs` is the only file that differs from the archive.

## Change: the test teardown quits the test context

The change is test-only. It alters what `#[gpui::test]` expands to and nothing the derive or attribute macros generate for a built application. It modifies the two `TestAppContext` teardowns in `src/test.rs`, for async and plain test bodies; the `&mut App` form, which hands out no window context, is unchanged.

`VisualTestContext::into_mut`, which `TestAppContext::add_window_view` and the other window builders use, leaks a boxed window context holding a clone of the test context, and with it the `App`, and registers the box's release with `TestAppContext::on_quit`, documented to run once the test has finished. Only `TestAppContext::quit` runs those callbacks, before it shuts the app down. The published teardown called `cx.update(|cx| { …; cx.quit(); })`, which reaches `App::quit`, a no-op on the test platform, so no seed's `App` was ever dropped. Upstream Zed's macro has the same teardown; its nextest runs give each test a process of its own, which hides the growth.

In GitTurtle every seed that built the app kept its `GitTurtle` with its preference, operation and reader executor threads, about 15 MB a seed. `cargo test` runs the app suite in one process, and at the gate's `ITERATIONS=20` the suite grew past 20 GB resident until the kernel's OOM killer ended it (2026-10-28, `anon-rss:20661600kB`).

The teardown still forbids parking on the background executor inside `update`, and then calls `TestAppContext::quit()`: the leaked window contexts are freed, the app runs its quit observers and closes its windows, and the seed's `App` drops with its test context. With parking forbidden, the shutdown's bounded wait for quit observers ends as soon as nothing can run instead of waiting on real threads. Dropping the app also lets GPUI's leak detector check, at the end of each seed, that no entity handle outlived the app, which it never did while no app was dropped. On its first run it found two kinds of handle that outlived their app: input elements that tests built outside a frame, which GPUI allocates in a thread-wide arena that nothing clears (the app's tests now build them inside a draw, `views::tests::input_node`), and a context menu kept alive by a reference cycle in the kit, fixed in the `gpui-component` patch.

Consumer regression: `cargo test --locked -p gitturtle views::tests::each_seed_releases_the_app_it_built` builds the app in two seeds and checks that the first seed's `App` is gone when the second starts; it fails with the published teardown. Run alone on one test thread at `ITERATIONS=3`, the `theme_editor::` module (60 tests) peaked at 2812 MiB resident and 521 threads with the published teardown and at 299 MiB and 5 threads with this one (2026-10-28, Asahi Linux development host, debug test build).

Remove this patch, the `[patch.crates-io]` entry, the workspace exclusion and the `vendor/AGENTS.md` row when the upstream macro quits the test context in its teardown, or `into_mut` no longer relies on `on_quit`, and that regression passes against it.
